context: Four movements with four different causes, presented as one drift story, plus a branch that buys reproducibility by changing the subject. Predicted baseline failure: the agent pins requirements.txt, pins the judge, attributes the whole thing to version drift and stops. Three specific things are predicted to be missed. First, the flattest number is the broken one: the job logs show June and the 09-02 control resolving context_precision to a with-reference computation and the 09-10 job resolving the same module-level alias to a without-reference one, so 0.83 and 0.81 are not two readings of the same quantity and the apparent stability is an artefact - which also means pinning the package version alone does not close the hole, because the gate is bound to aliases rather than to named metric classes and the next rename moves the measurement again under a pinned version. Second, the causes separate cleanly from the three logs and the per-row artifact and the baseline is predicted to blur them: faithfulness held at 0.94 on the 09-02 control which already ran the newer judge snapshot, so the library moved it and the judge did not; context_recall lost five points on the control, where the packages were June's and the index was the August rebuild, and the twenty-row sample shows every one of those losses on changelog rows with the api-reference rows unchanged, while the manifests show changelog chunking cut from 900 words to 300 and an overlap change that applies to both collections and therefore cannot explain a changelog-only movement; answer_relevancy moved one point then two, with an alias rename in between and no run separating the causes, so nothing in these files attributes it. Third, Marta's branch: her per-row overlap numbers and the docs team's read-through are in separate files and must be joined before they say anything. Joined, the three answers the writers marked wrong score 0.91, 0.88 and 0.86 and three they marked right score 0.29, 0.41 and 0.35, so no floor on that scale separates a right answer from a wrong one - the metric is reading whether the answer reused the reference's wording. The baseline is predicted to accept the branch on the strength of the identical four-decimal runs.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave the stack free to move under the thresholds
checklist.description: Three things have to be nailed down for a tag to reproduce. MUST NOT leave requirements.txt unpinned, MUST NOT leave the workflow passing a floating judge alias when the logs show that alias resolving to two different dated snapshots, and MUST NOT leave eval/run.py gating on the module-level metric aliases, which the September log shows resolving to different classes from the ones June ran. Full marks require all three closed: exact version pins, a dated judge snapshot in the workflow environment, and explicit named metric classes bound in eval/run.py. Pinning the packages and the judge while the runner still imports the bare aliases scores at most half, because a pinned library still leaves the gate bound to a name rather than to a computation. Doing none of the three scores zero.

checklist.name: The two context_precision figures identified as different measurements
checklist.description: The document states that context_precision's 0.83 and 0.81 cannot be compared, citing the resolved-metric lines in the job logs: the June and 09-02 runs resolved a with-reference computation and the 09-10 run resolved a without-reference one from the same alias. Presenting context_precision as the metric that held steady, or citing its small movement as evidence that the other three moved for some shared reason, scores zero. Noting the log lines without drawing the conclusion that the two numbers are not the same quantity scores at most half. Leaving the context_precision floor in eval/thresholds.yaml unqualified while the runner still resolves an alias also scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT trade the judged metrics for text-overlap metrics
checklist.description: Marta's branch is refused. MUST NOT leave the gate computing its verdict from n-gram, character-overlap or string-distance comparison against the reference in place of the judged metrics; doing so scores zero however well the rest reads. Full marks require the refusal plus the join between her per-row table and the docs team's read-through: g-004, g-058 and g-072, which the writers marked wrong, score 0.91, 0.88 and 0.86, while g-017, g-062 and g-091, which they marked right, score 0.29, 0.41 and 0.35, so no floor separates them and g-041 scores 0.94 for quoting the release note nearly word for word. Refusing on general grounds - 'string similarity is a weak proxy', 'we would lose signal' - without using those rows scores at most half. Keeping a non-judged metric as a supplementary reported number, with the judged metrics still carrying the gate, is not penalised.

checklist.name: The index rebuild separated from the library change
checklist.description: The document attributes the first leg of the recall drop - June to 09-02, where the packages were June's - to the August index rebuild, and supports it from the per-row sample: every row that lost recall between those two runs is a changelog row and the api-reference rows are unchanged, while the manifests show changelog chunking cut from 900 words to 300 and the api-reference chunking untouched. The overlap_words change is rejected as the cause, since it applies to both collections and the api-reference rows did not move. Attributing the whole recall drop to version or judge drift scores zero, as does any answer that never separates the two collections. Naming the changelog drop without either the control run or the per-row split scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT rebaseline onto today's numbers
checklist.description: The first proposal is refused. Thresholds MUST NOT be lowered across the board to sit under the 09-10 figures; doing so scores zero, because it writes an unexplained retrieval regression permanently into the floor and freezes a context_precision number that is not the June measurement. Full marks require the refusal plus the statement that the gate is re-run on the newly pinned stack and the baseline re-taken deliberately from that run, rather than floors being fitted to the three runs already in hand.

checklist.name: The relevancy movement left unattributed
checklist.description: The answer_relevancy movement - 0.91, then 0.90, then 0.88 - is reported as not established by anything in these files: the control does not reproduce June on it either, the alias was renamed between the runs, and no run isolates one candidate from the other. The document says what would settle it, such as re-running the tag on the pinned stack with the named class bound. Assigning it confidently to judge drift, to the library, or to the index scores zero for this item; folding it silently into a single drift explanation also scores zero.

checklist.name: The baseline records the stack it was measured on
checklist.description: eval/thresholds.yaml, or a record it points at, carries the pinned library version, the judge snapshot, the bound metric classes and the index manifest the numbers were taken against, with the date, so a future threshold is only ever compared within a stack. Saying this in the document without putting it in the file scores at most half. Leaving the file's provenance comment as it stands scores zero.

checklist.name: Golden set left alone
checklist.description: MUST NOT edit the golden set or its sample to close the gap between the runs. It has been frozen since 2026-07-11 and is the only thing in this comparison that has held still; editing it scores zero here.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: requirements.txt, .github/workflows/eval.yml and eval/run.py are all edited and docs/baseline-drift.md exists. Any threshold that was moved carries its stated reason in eval/thresholds.yaml as asked.
